summary: Ephemeral session rotation mid-stream causes missing function-call confirmations and duplicate downstream side-effects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during long-lived streaming sessions they observed external tool side-effects executed twice or not at all after the client refreshed an ephemeral session token mid-stream. Impact: duplicate email sends and missing confirmation acks for time-sensitive ordering requests.

Impact:
- NimbleDocs observed 2x downstream webhook posts for ~7% of long-running sessions (approx 12 requests/hour).
- Some tool executions were never confirmed back to the client, leaving the UI in a 'pending' state.

Environment:
- Customer is on Dedicated capacity in us-east. They use our TypeScript SDK (v1.12.4) on the frontend and Python SDK (v0.9.8) in a server-side orchestrator.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Start a streaming function-call session (TS client) with ephemeral session token (issued by customer auth).
2) Midway through a long-running generation (~30s+), the client triggers a background token refresh which rotates the ephemeral session id used in Authorization and a custom 'x-session-id' header.
3) SDK automatically reconnects the stream using the new auth headers but does not preserve per-funcall confirmation metadata that was scoped to the prior session id.
4) On reconnect the server replays / retries pending funcalls; some confirmations race and are dropped by the orchestrator, others are re-executed (duplicate side-effects).

Observed logs (customer-provided):
- TS client trace: "stream reconnect: session-ephemeral-abc -> session-ephemeral-def"
- Serving runtime: "received funcall confirm for session-ephemeral-abc (no active session) -> ignoring"
- Orchestrator: "queued replay for pending-funcall-8923 (replay_count=1) -> executed webhook POST id=wx-773"

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Configure SDK to renew tokens before starting long-lived streams (shorten token refresh window) OR
- Include a per-funcall explicit idempotency token in the funcall payload (application-level) that is persisted across session refreshes.

Next steps requested:
- Engineering investigation to prevent replayed funcalls during session rotation and to surface clearer acks for orphaned confirmations.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Created ticket after receiving NimbleDocs incident report. Asked for sample traces and the exact SDK versions. Recommended immediate workaround: per-funcall idempotency token or shorten token refresh timing.
2026-03-10 11:05 - NimbleDocs (Customer): Provided traces and a minimal repro using TS SDK + server orchestrator. Noted duplicates only happen when refresh occurs during streaming generation >20s.

2026-03-10 14:30 - Jonah Kim (SRE): Reproduced locally with TS SDK v1.12.4 + python orchestrator. Observed session-id header mutated mid-stream and server treated replayed funcalls as new when confirmation header referenced old session id.

2026-03-11 08:00 - Elena Martinez (Runtime Eng): Initial hypothesis: session-scoped confirmation tokens are being keyed by ephemeral session id; when session rotates, those keys become unreachable and reconnect replay logic enqueues duplicates.

2026-03-11 13:50 - Jonah Kim (SRE): Added mitigation on edge: tolerate confirmation for previous session id for 60s and map them to the in-flight funcall id where possible. Pushed hotfix to staging for validation (PR #1789).

2026-03-12 10:15 - NimbleDocs (Customer): Applied app-level idempotency tokens per-funcall as interim; duplicates dropped to 0.5% but customer requests permanent fix as duplicates affect billing and user trust.
investigation_notes: Confirmed root cause: confirmation tokens and funcall in-flight state were indexed by ephemeral session id. Client-side session rotation invalidated the index and triggered server-side replay path that didn't reconcile prior confirmations.
Edge case: HTTP/2 stream multiplexing + connection reuse meant the reconnect sometimes reused underlying connection metadata, complicating header scoping in proxies.
Reproducible across SDKs: TS and Python repros succeeded. Go SDK not yet tested but likely affected if it uses same session header semantics.
Short-term mitigation implemented: allow mapping confirmations for previous session ids for up to 60s and prefer dedupe via per-funcall idempotency header when present.

Long-term fix candidates: (A) index in-flight funcalls by persistent request-id independent of ephemeral session id; (B) ensure SDKs propagate per-funcall idempotency token automatically across token refresh; (C) update proxy to preserve x-session-id consistently during mid-stream re-auth.
Related historical tickets: SUP-927411 had similar confirmation race but for chunk ack timing rather than session rotation. Link included for reference.
resolution: Mitigation deployed to staging: server-side mapping of confirmations from previous session id for 60s and improved replay dedupe when per-funcall idempotency token found. Customer recommended and adopted per-funcall idempotency tokens as a best practice.\n\nPlanned permanent work: create INT task to reindex in-flight funcalls by a persistent request id and update SDKs to auto-propagate an idempotency field during session refresh (see linked INT-4421).
follow_up_tasks: INT-4421: Reindex in-flight funcalls by persistent request id independent of ephemeral session id (Engineering)
INT-4430: SDK change - auto-propagate per-funcall idempotency token across token refreshes (SDK team: Python/TS/Go)
DOC-125: Update Streaming best-practices to recommend per-funcall idempotency and token-refresh patterns (DX)
MON-78: Add alert for funcall duplicate rate >1%/hour in serving runtime dashboards
